source_question.title: Regular3-polytopes of type{n,n}
source_question.locator: Conjecture3.7, PDFp11, renderedlines333–345; finite-group Definition2.2, renderedline107
source_question.paraphrase: For all d,n≥3 there exists a regular d-polytope of exact type{n,...,n}, a Coxeter quotient whose distinguished involutions satisfy the specified consecutive-triple power relations.
source_question.interpretation: Finite existence of a quotient is the literal assertion, using the source finite-group convention. Identification, order or IP of the whole universal presentation is a stronger, separately unproved claim except the classical n=3 case.
